idioms.meaning_en: Page 393 of 404 If he should recover [from the injury I inflicted on him with my arrow], then it is not because I blew on him [= put a spell on him, wishing him to become well]; and if he dies, then [considering the injury he sustained] it is only right that he should. (Making “arrow” the antecedent of the pronoun in would yield a slightly different meaning: “…then it is not because I charmed my arrow by blowing on it.”) Khansaa’ cries on account of Sakhr, and it is only right that she should, for she has seen distress at the hands of time; time inflicts great hurt indeed I was afraid – and there was reason for me to be afraid – that the Banu ‘Uqayl would depart, taking our neighbor [= poet’s beloved] with them And it is only appropriate that it [earth] should [do so]/and so it must [do]
